use FILTER clause to collapse multiple aggregate queries
optimized_sql:
SELECT
    CASE WHEN summary.cnt1 > 1071 THEN summary.avg_ext_tax1 ELSE summary.avg_net_paid1 END AS bucket1,
    CASE WHEN summary.cnt2 > 39161 THEN summary.avg_ext_tax2 ELSE summary.avg_net_paid2 END AS bucket2,
    CASE WHEN summary.cnt3 > 29434 THEN summary.avg_ext_tax3 ELSE summary.avg_net_paid3 END AS bucket3,
    CASE WHEN summary.cnt4 > 6568 THEN summary.avg_ext_tax4 ELSE summary.avg_net_paid4 END AS bucket4,
    CASE WHEN summary.cnt5 > 21216 THEN summary.avg_ext_tax5 ELSE summary.avg_net_paid5 END AS bucket5
FROM reason
JOIN (
    SELECT
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 1 AND 20) AS cnt1,
        avg(ss_ext_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 1 AND 20) AS avg_ext_tax1,
        avg(ss_net_paid_inc_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 1 AND 20) AS avg_net_paid1,
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 21 AND 40) AS cnt2,
        avg(ss_ext_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 21 AND 40) AS avg_ext_tax2,
        avg(ss_net_paid_inc_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 21 AND 40) AS avg_net_paid2,
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 41 AND 60) AS cnt3,
        avg(ss_ext_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 41 AND 60) AS avg_ext_tax3,
        avg(ss_net_paid_inc_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 41 AND 60) AS avg_net_paid3,
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 61 AND 80) AS cnt4,
        avg(ss_ext_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 61 AND 80) AS avg_ext_tax4,
        avg(ss_net_paid_inc_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 61 AND 80) AS avg_net_paid4,
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 81 AND 100) AS cnt5,
        avg(ss_ext_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 81 AND 100) AS avg_ext_tax5,
        avg(ss_net_paid_inc_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 81 AND 100) AS avg_net_paid5
    FROM store_sales
) AS summary ON reason.r_reason_sk = 1
WHERE reason.r_reason_sk = 1
